# CLI, MCP, and app channel reference

<!-- Generated by packages/mcp/src/reference.ts. Change that file or the definitions it reads, then run:
pnpm --filter @dohc/mcp exec vitest run src/reference.test.ts -u -->

Agents and developers use this page to work with dohc from outside the app. It lists every tool of the desktop MCP server, every `dohc` command, and every app channel request, with its arguments and what it returns.

## Connect

- **MCP.** In dohc, open **Settings**, then **Agents & MCP**. Choose **Enable MCP**, then copy the **MCP config** into your agent's MCP settings. The server works on one workspace.
- **CLI.** The `dohc` command talks to the running dohc app, so keep dohc open. Run it inside the workspace folder. Agents that dohc starts have it on their `PATH`.
- **Share links.** A share link has its own MCP server, `dohc-share`, with other tools. This page does not list them. The [share-web README](../../services/share-web/README.md) says how an agent connects to it.

## Versions and changes

Agent prompts and scripts depend on these names. Before launch, a rename replaces the old name outright, with no alias.

- The desktop MCP server reports its version as `0.3.0`. A rename or removal of a tool, argument, or result field raises it.
- `--json` output carries `schemaVersion: 2`. A change to the shape of that output raises it.
- The CLI and the app must be the same build. Otherwise the CLI stops with `CLI/app version mismatch — restart the app`.

A tool or command that cannot do what was asked returns `{ ok: false, reason }`, or exits with status 1 and prints the reason. MCP marks such a result as an error.

## Desktop MCP tools

### `dohc_dataset`

Create, prepare, approve, inspect, and use transactional Collections in the owning workspace. Apps bind to these same datasets; they have no separate private app store. Invoke approved operations with their described revision and a stable retry key. History shows record edits and schema/rule revisions. historyRevision reads immutable saved source. prepareHistoryRestore prepares a reviewed forward change against current records, preserving current access; approveMigration applies it. Source-file restoration alone never activates rules. Permissions manages explicit data grants. Export streams a private recovery archive to an explicit absolute savePath ending in .dohc-recovery; it includes private records, files, history, and retry credentials. Recovery uses prepareRecovery with explicit sourcePath, then claimRecovery after stopping the old host, or discardRecovery to cancel. The same rules apply in dohc and apps.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `request`: the JSON object of one [`dohc dataset`](#dohc-dataset) verb, with the verb's name as `action`. Required.

Returns what that verb returns, listed under [`dohc dataset`](#dohc-dataset).

### `dohc_list_workspaces`

List the local dohc workspaces in the desktop registry.

No arguments.

Returns `{ workspaces: { workspaceId, rootPath, kind, remote? }[] }`.

### `dohc_workspace_status`

Report whether this workspace is local-only or cloud-synced.

No arguments.

Returns `{ synced, scope, cloudConnected, credentialStatus, workspaceId?, serverUrl? }`. `scope` is `"local"` or `"cloud"`.

### `dohc_list_changes`

List workspace history, newest first: workspace-engine moments (the recorder for this workspace). Each entry carries path/operation/versionId. Pass path, relative to the workspace root, to list only that file's changes across its renames.

- `sinceMs`: `integer`
- `limit`: `integer`
- `includeFiles`: `boolean`
- `path`: `string`

Returns `{ changes: { id, recordedAtMs, source: "workspace-engine", operation, path, versionId, author?, fileCount: 1, files? }[], count, totalAvailable, hasMore, cursorMs }`.

### `dohc_read_change`

Read one history entry by id: a workspace-engine moment with its full before/after payload.

- `id`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, change: { id, recordedAtMs, source: "workspace-engine", operation, path, versionId, author?, fileCount: 1, files, before, after } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_files`

List visible files and folders in the workspace. Hidden dohc internals are omitted.

- `path`: `string`
- `recursive`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, root, entries: { path, kind, bytes?, mediaType? }[] }`.

### `dohc_read_file`

Read any visible workspace file as UTF-8 text or base64, returning size and sha256 for safe follow-up writes.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `encoding`: `"utf8" | "base64"`
- `maxBytes`: `integer`
- `offsetBytes`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, mediaType, encoding, bytes, offsetBytes, sha256, truncated, content }`.

### `dohc_search_files`

Search visible workspace file paths and text contents. Hidden dohc internals, .git, node_modules, symlinks, oversized files, and binary files are skipped.

- `query`: `string`. Required.
- `path`: `string`
- `mode`: `"content" | "path" | "both"`
- `caseSensitive`: `boolean`
- `regex`: `boolean`
- `maxResults`: `integer`
- `maxFileBytes`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, query, root, mode, matches: { type, path, mediaType?, line?, column?, preview }[], matchCount, limitHit, skipped: { path, reason }[] }`.

### `dohc_read_document`

Read a Markdown document as it is now, including edits an open editor has not saved to the file yet. Read it before dohc_edit_document: edits match this text.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, markdown } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_edit_document`

Edit a Markdown document through dohc. A person editing it at the same time keeps their text and sees yours arrive. While someone may be typing in it, in an open editor or on a device it syncs to, an edit may change text inside blocks and add blocks, but not remove a block or change its kind. `find` is Markdown that occurs exactly once in the text dohc_read_document returns; it becomes `replacement`. Omit `find` to add `replacement` at the end. The edit changes the body, not the frontmatter. It returns when the edit is saved. A `warning` means someone may be changing the document at the same moment, and their change to the same blocks can still remove your text; read the document to check. `requestId` is a random key you choose, such as a UUID. Sent again with the same key, after a timeout for example, the edit returns its first result instead of applying twice, while it runs and until 1,024 later keyed requests to this workspace have finished. dohc then refuses the key until 16,384 more have finished; after that, or after dohc restarts, the key can apply the edit again. Use a new key for each new edit, including one that redoes text a failed edit reported missing. If the call fails without a reason, read the document before you retry.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `find`: `string`
- `replacement`: `string`. Required.
- `requestId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, changed, warning? } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_create_document`

Create a Markdown document at a path that does not exist yet. `markdown` is its body text, without frontmatter. dohc writes it the way a person types into a new file, so later changes go through dohc_edit_document.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `markdown`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_write_file`

Write an ordinary workspace file. Markdown documents are created with dohc_create_document and changed with dohc_edit_document, and Excalidraw scenes change in dohc; this tool refuses both. The desktop watcher captures file history while open, or on the next open.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `content`: `string`. Required.
- `encoding`: `"utf8" | "base64"`
- `expectedSha256`: `string`
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, bytes, sha256, recordedBy }`.

### `dohc_create_directory`

Create a visible workspace directory. Files later written inside it are captured as engine moments by the desktop watcher.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, recordedBy }`, or `{ ok: true, path, unchanged: true }` when the folder exists.

### `dohc_move_path`

Move or rename a visible workspace file/folder. The desktop watcher captures the change as engine moments while the app is open.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `fromPath`: `string`. Required.
- `toPath`: `string`. Required.
- `overwrite`: `boolean`
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, fromPath, toPath, recordedBy }`.

### `dohc_delete_path`

Delete a visible workspace file/folder by moving it to dohc's recoverable trash. The desktop watcher captures the delete as an engine moment while the app is open.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `summary`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, trashed: true, recordedBy }`.

### `dohc_detect_apps`

Detect app folders in the workspace: web content a browser can open, found from index.html, package.json, dohc.json, and common web configs.

- `path`: `string`
- `maxDepth`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, apps: { root, title, kind, confidence, entry?, packageManager?, scripts, configuredPreviewMode?, buildOutputs, configPath?, diagnostics }[], count, detector }`.

### `dohc_create_app`

Scaffold an app folder with index.html, package.json, a pinned serve devDependency, and an optional dohc.json. Records history; does not create hidden app folders.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.
- `title`: `string`
- `withDohcJson`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, appRoot, files, recordedBy }`.

### `dohc_test_app`

Run bounded static validation for an app folder: detector diagnostics and entry presence.

- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok, app, checks: { name, ok, message?, path? }[] }`. `ok` is true when every check passes.

### `dohc_import_data`

Import a CSV/JSON/JSONL/Markdown source into a new visible .sqlite database.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `sourcePath`: `string`. Required.
- `databasePath`: `string`. Required.
- `tableName`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, tableName, rowCount, recordedBy }`.

### `dohc_query_database`

Run a single read-only SELECT against a visible workspace database (bounded rows).

- `databasePath`: `string`. Required.
- `sql`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, rows }`, with at most 1,000 rows.

### `dohc_list_file_chats`

List the dohc Chats linked to a workspace file. Chats follow the file's stable dohc identity across renames. Requires the workspace engine.

- `path`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, path, fileObjectId, threads: { id, title, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, linkedPathHint? }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_chat`

Read one dohc Chat thread: its messages (with author kind and display name), dispatch pause state and latest run outcome, and a read-only text projection.

- `threadId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, thread: { id, title, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, linkedPathHint? }, dispatch: { paused, lastRun }, messages: { id, threadId, authorKind, authorDisplayName, authorOwnerDisplayName?, body, createdAtMs, parentMessageId?, attachments, needsDecision, decisionState?, options?, chosenOption?, resolvedByMessageId? }[], projection: { path, readOnly: true, text } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_groups`

List the workspace's Chats groups (including the default #general) with each group's chats and their ids. It also returns direct messages and the agent lane, told apart by `kind`. Requires the workspace engine.

No arguments.

Returns `{ ok: true, groups: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose?, threadCount, threads }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_start_group_chat`

Start a new chat in a group as the agent. `group` accepts a group name, #slug, or id. No title needed; the chat displays its first message. `attachments` are workspace-relative paths of tracked files; `needsDecision` asks for a decision and `options` turns it into a poll; `runId` links the message to a local agent run. Returns engine ids usable with dohc_read_chat.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `group`: `string`. Required.
- `title`: `string`
- `body`: `string`. Required.
- `attachments`: `string[]`
- `needsDecision`: `boolean`
- `options`: `string[]`
- `runId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, group: { id, slug, kind }, threadId, messageId, title, warning? }`.

### `dohc_start_file_chat`

Comment on a workspace file as the agent. This starts a chat linked to the file, as a person does from the file's Chats panel: `title` names the chat there and `body` is its first message. dohc_list_file_chats returns it, and dohc_reply_to_chat continues it. `requestId` is a random key you choose, such as a UUID. Sent again with the same key, after a timeout for example, the comment returns its first result instead of starting a second chat, while it runs and until 1,024 later keyed requests to this workspace have finished. dohc then refuses the key until 16,384 more have finished; after that, or after dohc restarts, the key can start another chat. `runId` behaves as in dohc_start_group_chat.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `path`: `string`. Required.
- `title`: `string`. Required.
- `body`: `string`. Required.
- `requestId`: `string`
- `runId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, path, threadId, messageId, warning? } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_reply_to_chat`

Reply in a dohc Chat thread as the agent. `to` replies under one message; `resolve` closes that open decision with this reply and `choose` names the option picked. Message ids come from dohc_read_chat. `attachments`, `needsDecision`, `options`, and `runId` behave as in dohc_start_group_chat.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `threadId`: `string`. Required.
- `to`: `string`
- `resolve`: `string`
- `choose`: `string`
- `body`: `string`. Required.
- `attachments`: `string[]`
- `needsDecision`: `boolean`
- `options`: `string[]`
- `runId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, threadId, messageId, parentMessageId?, resolvedMessageId?, warning? }`.

### `dohc_query_collection`

Query a collection folder's indexed records: filter, sort, group, and page. Requires the workspace engine and the dohc app.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `filter`: `{ field: string, operator: "equals" | "contains", value: any JSON }`
- `sort`: `({ field: string, direction: "asc" | "desc" })[]`
- `groupBy`: `string`
- `resolveRelations`: `boolean`
- `limit`: `integer`
- `cursor`: `any JSON`

Returns `{ ok: true, collection: { path, status, reasons }, records: { id, path, conflicted, values }[], groups: { value, records }[] | null, nextCursor: { sortValues, recordPath, recordId } | null } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_record`

Read one collection record by id: current field values plus per-field history with author attribution. Requires the workspace engine and the dohc app.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `recordId`: `string`. Required.
- `historyLimit`: `integer`
- `beforeHistoryId`: `integer`

Returns `{ ok: true, collection: { path, status, reasons }, record: { id, path, conflicted, values }, history: { historyId, field, previous, next, authorOriginId, actorKind, onBehalfOf, depth, recordedAtMs }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_set_record_fields`

Set fields on a collection record as the agent, e.g. fields: {"status": "done"}. The change lands in the record's live frontmatter, open desktop views update, and record history attributes it to the agent.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `recordPath`: `string`. Required.
- `fields`: `{ [key: string]: any JSON }`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, recordPath } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_create_record`

Create a Markdown record in a collection folder as the agent, optionally seeding fields, and return its record id. A name already taken in the folder is refused.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `name`: `string`. Required.
- `fields`: `{ [key: string]: any JSON }`

Returns `{ ok: true, recordId, recordPath } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_list_automation_runs`

List an automation's 20 newest runs on this computer, newest first: each run's id, state, what started it, how many changes it made, and why it failed. Name the automation by its Collection's folder and its id in automations.yaml. Each computer keeps the runs of the automations it ran.

A shared view keeps no automation runs, so it does not offer this tool.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `automation`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, runs: { run, state, error, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, trigger, definitionChanged, chainStopped, undone, changes }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_read_automation_run`

Read one automation run: what started it, what each step changed, why it failed, which step failed, and whether Try again resumes there or starts over. Steps count from 1 in the order automations.yaml lists them, including the steps inside if and otherwise. A step that changed nothing is not listed.

A shared view keeps no automation runs, so it does not offer this tool.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `automation`: `string`. Required.
- `run`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ ok: true, run: { run, state, error, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, trigger, definitionChanged, chainStopped, undone, steps, failedStep, startsOver } } | { ok: false, reason }`.

### `dohc_retry_automation_run`

Try a failed automation run again, as Try again does in dohc. It resumes after the last step that finished. If the automation changed since the run failed, it refuses unless startOver is true, which runs it from the first step and can repeat changes the run already made. Only the computer that ran it can try a run again; anywhere else the refusal names that computer.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `automation`: `string`. Required.
- `run`: `string`. Required.
- `startOver`: `boolean`

Returns `{ ok: true, status: "queued" } | { ok: false, status, repeatsMessages, reason } | { ok: false, reason, notice?: { title, body } }`.

### `dohc_press_button`

Press a Button field on one record, as a person clicks it in dohc, and get the id of the run it started; follow it with dohc_read_automation_run. Name the record by its id, or a dataset record by its primary key as JSON. A press that would run actions dohc cannot undo is refused with each action's name; press again with those names in confirm to run them. Send the same requestId again, after a timeout for example, to get the same press instead of a second one. The press is recorded as the agent's, for the person; from an agent run that an automation started, it counts in that chain of automations, which stops after 4 steps.

Changes the workspace, so a shared view does not offer it.

- `collectionPath`: `string`. Required.
- `button`: `string`. Required.
- `recordId`: `string`. Required.
- `table`: `string`
- `confirm`: `string[]`
- `requestId`: `string`

Returns `{ ok: true, run, outcome, error, waiting } | { ok: true, relayed: true } | { ok: false, reason, confirm: { name, label }[] } | { ok: false, reason }`.

## CLI

```sh
dohc <command> <verb> [arguments] [options]
```

`dohc --help`, `dohc <command> --help`, and `dohc <command> <verb> --help` print the same summaries, flags, and fields as this section. These options work with every verb:

- `--as-agent`: Post and read chat as an agent.
- `--json`: Print the result as JSON.
- `--help`: Show help. -h does the same.

Two environment variables also change what the CLI does:

- `DOHC_RUN_ID` links the messages that `post` and `reply` write to a local agent run.
- `DOHC_STATE_DIR` names the app's state folder when the CLI cannot find the running app in its default place.

### `dohc document`

Read, edit, and create live Markdown documents.

Paths resolve from your current folder. Changes are recorded as an agent's, as with MCP. A refusal exits with status 1 and prints its reason to stderr, including with --json.

#### `dohc document read`

```sh
dohc document read <path> [options]
```

Read the current Markdown, including edits in an open editor.

Read before editing. Without --json, prints the Markdown byte for byte.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, markdown }`.

#### `dohc document edit`

```sh
dohc document edit <path> [-] [options]
```

Replace matching text or append Markdown through the live document.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. Use --text instead to supply the body as an argument. Each side allows at most 256 KiB of UTF-8. Edits change the body, not frontmatter. Concurrent editing can prevent removing blocks or changing their kind. Read again after a warning or an unexplained failure. Retry keys have the same limits as dohc_edit_document.

- `--text <markdown>`: Use this Markdown as the body. An empty string is allowed.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name with the change.
- `--find <markdown>`: Replace this exact, unique match. Omit to append.
- `--request-id <key>`: Reuse this key when retrying the same edit, as with dohc_edit_document.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path, changed, warning? }`.

#### `dohc document create`

```sh
dohc document create <path> [-] [options]
```

Create a Markdown document without overwriting an existing file.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. Use --text instead to supply Markdown. With neither, create an empty document. The path must end in .md or .markdown. Frontmatter is refused.

- `--text <markdown>`: Use this Markdown as the body. An empty string is allowed.
- `--agent <name>`: Record this agent name with the change.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, path }`.

### `dohc chat`

Read and post in Groups and threads.

Name a Group by its name or ID, and a thread or message by its ID. A unique ID prefix also works. DOHC_CHAT_ACTOR=agent in the environment does the same as --as-agent.

#### `dohc chat groups`

```sh
dohc chat groups [options]
```

List the Groups in this workspace.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, groups: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose? }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat threads`

```sh
dohc chat threads <group> [options]
```

List the threads in a Group.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, group: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose? }, threads: { lane?, id, title, commentCount, openDecisionCount, unread, updatedAtMs }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat inbox`

```sh
dohc chat inbox [options]
```

List unread threads. For an agent, also list its unread mentions.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, threads: { lane?, id, title, commentCount, openDecisionCount, unread, updatedAtMs, group }[], mentions: { threadId, messageId, group, author, createdAtMs, text }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat show`

```sh
dohc chat show <thread-or-message> [options]
```

Show a thread or message and mark the thread read.

- `--peek`: Show it without changing what is marked read. A read-only shared view requires it.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, thread: { id, title, group, commentCount, openDecisionCount }, dispatch: { paused, lastRun }, messages: { id, author, body, createdAtMs, parentMessageId?, decisionState?, decisionOptions?, decisionChosenOption?, attachments, runId? }[] }`.

#### `dohc chat post`

```sh
dohc chat post <group> <body> [options]
```

Start a thread in a Group.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. In a direct message, use reply instead. Put options first, then --, then text that starts with a dash.

- `--title <title>`: Set the thread's title.
- `--attach <path>`: Attach a workspace file. Repeat for more files.
- `--needs-decision`: Ask readers for a decision.
- `--option <choice>`: Offer a choice. Repeat for more choices. Implies --needs-decision.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, group: { kind, id, name, slug, purpose? }, threadId, messageId, title, warning? }`.

#### `dohc chat reply`

```sh
dohc chat reply <thread> <body> [options]
```

Reply in a thread.

Use - as the body to read it from stdin. Put options first, then --, then text that starts with a dash.

- `--to <message>`: Reply to this message in the thread.
- `--attach <path>`: Attach a workspace file. Repeat for more files.
- `--needs-decision`: Ask readers for a decision.
- `--option <choice>`: Offer a choice. Repeat for more choices. Implies --needs-decision.
- `--resolve <message>`: Resolve this open decision with the reply.
- `--choose <choice>`: Pick this choice of the decision. Needs --resolve.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, threadId, messageId, parentMessageId?, resolvedMessageId?, warning? }`.

#### `dohc chat react`

```sh
dohc chat react <message> <emoji> [options]
```

Add your reaction to a message, or remove it if it is already there.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, threadId, messageId, emoji, state }`.

#### `dohc chat grep`

```sh
dohc chat grep <pattern> [options]
```

Search message text and thread titles.

Put options first, then --, then text that starts with a dash.

- `--group <group>`: Search only this Group.
- `--thread <thread>`: Search only this thread.
- `--from <author>`: Match authors: human, agent, or part of a name.
- `--since <when>`: Match messages newer than a date or an age such as 7d.
- `-i`: Ignore case. Without it, a regex or a pattern with capitals matches case.
- `-l`: Print only the IDs of threads that match.
- `-C <count>`: Show this many messages before and after each match.
- `--limit <count>`: Print at most this many results. The default is 100.
- `--regex`: Read the pattern as a regular expression.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, matches: { group, threadId, messageId, author, createdAtMs, text, contextBefore, contextAfter }[] }` or `{ schemaVersion, threadIds }`.

#### `dohc chat export`

```sh
dohc chat export [options]
```

Save threads as Markdown files, one file per thread.

Use at most one of --all, --group, or --thread.

- `--out <folder>`: Write the files to this folder. Required.
- `--all`: Export every thread. This is the default.
- `--group <group>`: Export the threads in one Group.
- `--thread <thread>`: Export one thread.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, files: { threadId, path }[] }`.

### `dohc dataset`

```sh
dohc dataset <verb> '<JSON>'
```

Create, change, and use transactional Collections.

Each verb takes one JSON object that names workspaceId. Find workspaceId in .dohc/manifest.json at the workspace root. These verbs use the same Collection rules as dohc. They do not accept SQL or caller identity.

#### `dohc dataset list`

List Collections.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `after`: `UUID`
- `limit`: `integer`
- `includeArchived`: `boolean`

Returns `{ kind: "list", datasets, nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc dataset describe`

Show a Collection's tables, fields, and operations.

Use describe to find approved operation IDs.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `includeArchived`: `boolean`

Returns `{ kind: "description", dataset, copy?: { offline, savedAtMs, coverage?: "saved-pages" } }`.

#### `dohc dataset history`

List saved operations, with values to undo edits.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `beforeRevision`: `integer`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "history", datasetId, headRevision, entries: { revision, operation, callerReference, recordedAtMs, approvedRevisionHash, changesetBytes, attachmentCount, undo?, automation?, schema? }[], nextBeforeRevision }`.

#### `dohc dataset historyRevision`

Show the saved source of one past revision.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `revisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "history-revision", revision, schemaSql, operationSource }`.

#### `dohc dataset prepareHistoryRestore`

Prepare a change that reverses one saved change.

Set `targetRevisionSha256` to `entries[].schema.previousRevisionHash` from `history`. Set `changedRevisionSha256` to `entries[].schema.revisionHash` from `history`. Review the result, then approve it with approveMigration.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `revision`: `integer`. Required.
- `revisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `targetRevisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `changedRevisionSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "migration-prepared", preparationId, previousRevision, revision, expected: { workspaceId, datasetId, hostEpoch, approvedRevisionHash, revision, digest }, candidate: { candidateId, expected, approvedRevisionHash, checkpointSha256, expiresAtMs, preview }, sourceDigest, approvalDigest, schemaSql, operationSource, migrationSql, expiresAtMs }`.

#### `dohc dataset permissions`

List app bindings and explicit data grants.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `after`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "permissions", permissions: ({ kind: "data", principal, current, metadata } | { kind: "app", principal, current, metadata })[], nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc dataset setGrant`

Add or change an explicit data grant.

grant names revision, revisionSha256, operationIds, and discover.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `grantId`: `string`. Required.
- `grant`: `{ revision: integer, revisionSha256: SHA-256 hex, operationIds: UUID[], discover: boolean }`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "grant-updated" }`.

#### `dohc dataset removeGrant`

Remove an explicit data grant.

Set `principalKey` to `permissions[].principal` from `permissions`.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `principalKey`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "grant-updated" }`.

#### `dohc dataset lifecycle`

Show a Collection's archive state and its apps.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `after`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "lifecycle", archived, generation, reason, apps: { appId, binding }[], nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc dataset archive`

Stop a Collection's operations and keep its records.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "lifecycle-updated", archived, generation, reason? }`.

#### `dohc dataset restore`

Restore an archived Collection under its rules.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "lifecycle-updated", archived, generation, reason? }`.

#### `dohc dataset deletePreview`

Review what deleting a Collection affects.

The result lists affected apps and holds what delete needs.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `after`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "delete-preview", archived, generation, reason, apps: { appId, binding }[], nextCursor, cursor: { workspaceId, datasetId, hostEpoch, approvedRevisionHash, revision, digest }, reviewToken, name, irreversible: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset delete`

Permanently delete a Collection and all its data.

Set `expected` to `cursor` from `deletePreview`. Set `reviewToken` to `reviewToken` from `deletePreview`. This removes the Collection's private data and history. Set acknowledge to true. Export before deleting if you need a recovery copy. Deleted Collections cannot be restored in place.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `expected`: `{ workspaceId: string, datasetId: UUID, hostEpoch: string, approvedRevisionHash: SHA-256 hex, revision: integer, digest: SHA-256 hex }`. Required.
- `reviewToken`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `acknowledge`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "deleted", deleted: true, datasetId }`.

#### `dohc dataset pendingAttempts`

List pending responses that still hold a retry.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `after`: `integer`
- `limit`: `integer`

Returns `{ kind: "pending-attempts", datasetId, entries: { reference, operation, recordedAtMs, revision, outcome, attachmentCount }[], nextAfter }`.

#### `dohc dataset reconcileAttempt`

Clear the retry of a saved pending response.

Set `reference` to `entries[].reference` from `pendingAttempts`. Set acknowledge to true. This cannot be undone.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `reference`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `acknowledge`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "attempt-reconciled", cleared: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset cancelAttempt`

Cancel an unconfirmed pending response.

Set `reference` to `entries[].reference` from `pendingAttempts`. Set acknowledge to true.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `reference`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `acknowledge`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "attempt-cancelled", cancelled: true }`.

#### `dohc dataset export`

Save a private recovery archive of a Collection.

savePath is an absolute path ending in .dohc-recovery. Set overwrite to true to replace a file. Recovery archives contain private records, uploaded files, history, and retry credentials. Store them privately.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `savePath`: `string`. Required.
- `overwrite`: `boolean`

Returns `{ kind: "exported", savedPath }`.

#### `dohc dataset prepareRecovery`

Check a recovery archive before restoring it.

sourcePath is an absolute path ending in .dohc-recovery. Review the result before claimRecovery.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `sourcePath`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "recovery-prepared", recovery: { transferId, manifestSha256, sourceCursor, revision } | null }`.

#### `dohc dataset claimRecovery`

Restore a Collection from a prepared archive.

Set `workspaceId` to `recovery.sourceCursor.workspaceId` from `prepareRecovery`. Set `datasetId` to `recovery.sourceCursor.datasetId` from `prepareRecovery`. Set `transferId` to `recovery.transferId` from `prepareRecovery`. Set `manifestSha256` to `recovery.manifestSha256` from `prepareRecovery`. Set `sourceCursor` to `recovery.sourceCursor` from `prepareRecovery`. Stop the old host first, then set oldHostStopped to true. Copy only these fields.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `datasetId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `transferId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `manifestSha256`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `sourceCursor`: `{ workspaceId: string, datasetId: UUID, hostEpoch: string, approvedRevisionHash: SHA-256 hex, revision: integer, digest: SHA-256 hex }`. Required.
- `oldHostStopped`: `true`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "recovery-claimed", transferId, manifestSha256, sourceCursor: { workspaceId, datasetId, hostEpoch, approvedRevisionHash, revision, digest }, targetCursor: { workspaceId, datasetId, hostEpoch, approvedRevisionHash, revision, digest } }`.

#### `dohc dataset discardRecovery`

Cancel a prepared recovery before it installs.

Set `transferId` to `recovery.transferId` from `prepareRecovery`.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `transferId`: `UUID`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "recovery-discarded" }`.

Required.

Returns `{ kind: "migration-prepared", preparationId, previousRevision, revision, expected: { workspaceId, datasetId, hostEpoch, approvedRevisionHash, revision, digest }, candidate: { candidateId, expected, approvedRevisionHash, checkpointSha256, expiresAtMs, preview }, sourceDigest, approvalDigest, schemaSql, operationSource, migrationSql, expiresAtMs }`.

### `dohc app`

```sh
dohc app <verb> '<JSON>'
```

Approve, open, and share apps.

Each verb takes one JSON object that names workspaceId. Find workspaceId in .dohc/manifest.json at the workspace root.

#### `dohc app listLocal`

List an app's publications on this computer.

- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "localListed", publications: { publicationId, authorityRevision, appRoot, sourceRevision, active, datasetCapability }[] }`.

#### `dohc app prepareLocal`

Prepare an app to open on this computer.

Review the source and the dataset operations it asks for, then approve.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "prepared", approvalId, candidateDigest, appRoot, versionId, sourceRevision, sourcePaths, capabilities, externalNetwork: true, local?: true }`.

#### `dohc app launchLocal`

Get a local URL for an approved app.

The URL works on this computer while dohc is open. It is not a share link.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `publicationId`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "localLaunched", publicationId, url }`.

#### `dohc app list`

List an app's shared publications.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.
- `cursor`: `SHA-256 hex`

Returns `{ kind: "listed", publications: ({ publicationId, authorityRevision, shareId, grantId, active, linkCurrent, collectionCapability, datasetCapability, manifestUnavailable: false, appRoot, sourceRevision } | { publicationId, authorityRevision, shareId, grantId, active, linkCurrent, collectionCapability, datasetCapability, manifestUnavailable: true })[], nextCursor }`.

#### `dohc app prepare`

Prepare an app for a share link.

shareId and grantId name the share and its link grant. Review the result, then approve.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `appRoot`: `string`. Required.
- `shareId`: `string`. Required.
- `grantId`: `string`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "prepared", approvalId, candidateDigest, appRoot, versionId, sourceRevision, sourcePaths, capabilities, externalNetwork: true, local?: true }`.

#### `dohc app approve`

Publish a prepared app.

Take approvalId and candidateDigest from prepare, prepareLocal, or reviewReactivation.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `approvalId`: `UUID`. Required.
- `candidateDigest`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `linkReads`: `({ operationId: UUID, fieldIds: UUID[] })[]`

Returns `{ kind: "published", publicationId, authorityRevision, local?: true }`.

#### `dohc app cancel`

Discard a prepared app before approval.

Returns `{ kind: "cancelled" }`.

#### `dohc app withdraw`

Stop a shared publication.

Set `publicationId` to `publications[].publicationId` from `list`. Set `expectedAuthorityRevision` to `publications[].authorityRevision` from `list`.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `publicationId`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `expectedAuthorityRevision`: `integer`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "withdrawn", publicationId, authorityRevision }`.

#### `dohc app revokeCollection`

Remove a shared publication's Collection access.

Set `publicationId` to `publications[].publicationId` from `list`. Set `expectedAuthorityRevision` to `publications[].authorityRevision` from `list`.

- `workspaceId`: `string`. Required.
- `publicationId`: `SHA-256 hex`. Required.
- `expectedAuthorityRevision`: `integer`. Required.

Returns `{ kind: "collectionRevoked", publicationId, authorityRevision }`.

Prepare a stopped publication to publish again.

Returns `{ kind: "prepared", approvalId, candidateDigest, appRoot, versionId, sourceRevision, sourcePaths, capabilities, externalNetwork: true, local?: true }`.

### `dohc history`

Read the changes History records for files.

Changes come from the active version of the workspace.

#### `dohc history list`

```sh
dohc history list [<path>] [options]
```

List changes to files, newest first.

With a path, list that file's own changes, across its renames. Each line starts with the change's ID.

- `--limit <count>`: List at most this many changes. The default is 50, the most 500.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, changes: { id, recordedAtMs, source: "workspace-engine", operation, path, versionId, author?, fileCount: 1, files? }[], count, totalAvailable, hasMore, cursorMs }`.

#### `dohc history show`

```sh
dohc history show <change> [options]
```

Print a file's text as one change left it.

Find the change's ID with history list. With --json, print both sides and the change's details.

- `--before`: Print the text from before the change instead.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, change: { id, recordedAtMs, source: "workspace-engine", operation, path, versionId, author?, fileCount: 1, files, before, after } }`.

### `dohc automation`

Press Button fields, read an automation's runs, and try a failed run again.

Name a Collection by its folder in the workspace, and an automation by its id in the Collection's automations.yaml. Each computer keeps the runs of the automations it ran. Try again follows the same rules as in dohc.

#### `dohc automation runs`

```sh
dohc automation runs <collection> <automation> [options]
```

List an automation's runs on this computer, newest first.

Lists the 20 newest runs, as the Automations panel does. Each line starts with the run's ID.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, runs: { run, state, error, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, trigger, definitionChanged, chainStopped, undone, changes }[] }`.

#### `dohc automation run`

```sh
dohc automation run <collection> <automation> <run> [options]
```

Show one run: what started it, what each step changed, and why it failed.

Steps count from 1 in the order automations.yaml lists them, including the steps inside if and otherwise. A step that changed nothing is not listed.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, run: { run, state, error, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, trigger, definitionChanged, chainStopped, undone, steps, failedStep, startsOver } }`.

#### `dohc automation retry`

```sh
dohc automation retry <collection> <automation> <run> [options]
```

Try a failed run again. It resumes after the last step that finished.

Only the computer that ran it can try a run again. Anywhere else, the command names that computer.

- `--start-over`: Run it from the first step when the automation changed since the run failed. This can repeat changes the run already made.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, status: "queued" }`.

#### `dohc automation press`

```sh
dohc automation press <collection> <button> <record> [options]
```

Press a Button field on one record, as a person clicks it in dohc.

Name the record by its id, or a dataset record by its primary key as JSON. The press prints the id of the run it started. Follow it with automation run. With --as-agent, the press is recorded as the agent's, for you. A press from an agent run that an automation started is the agent's too, and counts in that chain of automations, which stops after 4 steps. In a shared view, a press goes to the owner's computer, which runs it, as in dohc.

- `--table <table>`: Name the table when the button is in more than one table of a dataset Collection.
- `--confirm <action>`: Run this action, which dohc cannot undo. The press names each action it would run. Repeat for more actions.
- `--request-id <id>`: Send the same id again, after a timeout for example, to get the same press instead of a second one.

With `--json`, prints `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, run, outcome, error, waiting }` or `{ schemaVersion, ok: true, relayed: true }`.

## App channel

An app page reads and changes its Collection through the app channel. The channel works in two places: a published app opened from a share link, and a local app opened with `dohc app launchLocal`. An app open in a dohc tab has no channel.

When the page loads, its parent window posts `{ kind: "dohc-app-channel", version: 1 }` with one `MessagePort`. The page keeps that port and posts each request to it as `{ id, op, ...fields }`. `id` is 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_`, or `-`, and no two requests in flight share one. The port answers `{ id, ok: true, value }`, or `{ id, ok: false, status }` with status 400, 404, 409, 413, 429, or 503. At most four requests can wait at once.

The app calls only the operations its owner approved when publishing it. `app.publish.json` names them under `dataset.operationIds`. The page never sends a workspace, user, or revision, because the host supplies them.

### `backend.invoke`

Calls one operation the app's publication exposes, by name. Reads use it too, with a new `idempotencyKey` for each call. Retry an uncertain write with the same `input` and `idempotencyKey`.

Fields: `operation`, `input`, `idempotencyKey`.

Answers `{ result, revision, replayed }`. A refusal from the operation arrives as status 409 with `error: { code, message }`.

### `backend.upload`

Uploads one file, at most 5 MiB, for a later operation to attach.

Fields: `name`, `contentType`, `bytesBase64`, `idempotencyKey`.

Answers `{ file, replayed }`.

### `backend.file`

Reads an uploaded file through an exposed read operation.

Fields: `fileId`, `operation`, `input`.

Answers `{ file, bytesBase64 }`.

### `backend.attempt`

Saves, reads, or clears one unconfirmed submission for an operation, so the page can retry it after a reload. `request` is `{ action: "get" }`, `{ action: "save", idempotencyKey, input }`, or `{ action: "clear", token }`.

Fields: `operation`, `request`.

Answers `{ attempt: { token, idempotencyKey, input } | null }`.

### `collection.list`

Lists records of the document Collection a published app binds to, at most 100 at a time. Add `afterPath` to read the next page. Only a published app opened from a share link can send it.

Fields: `limit`.

Answers `{ records: { path, recordId, fields }[], nextPath }`.

### `collection.create`

Adds a record to that Collection. Only a published app opened from a share link can send it.

Fields: `fields`, `idempotencyKey`.

Answers `{ kind: "accepted", acceptanceId, acceptedAtMs, momentId, objectId, path }`.
